text:
Maria Gomez: Heads up — after the 03:00 deploy I'm seeing p99 jump on long-seq jobs (12k-16k). Not steady CPU; looks like a tail-surge that correlates with KV cache churn.
Devin Khatri: +1 saw the same in the dashboard. p95 is fine but p99 up ~220ms on avg. Any recent kernel routing changes? :thinking:
Liam O'Connell: We pushed a kernel-selection tweak that prefers fused attn kernels for >=8k tokens. Might be triggering slower fallback paths when microbatching interacts with KV eviction.
Akash Patel: BenchBot ran a controlled replay overnight. BenchBot: perf-run: replay 1.2M tokens; baseline vs post-deploy: median +5ms, p95 +40ms, p99 +210ms, tail-0.1% +480ms.
Maria Gomez: Thanks bench data. I'm worried it's the combination: larger seq -> kernel choice -> larger kernel init cost + microbatching queues -> then timeouts/truncation kicks in.
Ryan SRE: We should avoid hard p99 regressions for hosted SLO routes. Quick mitigation options: (a) per-route max_tokens cap, (b) aggressive truncation/prefix-drop for extremely long prompts, (c) shorter microbatch caps for long sequences, (d) fallback to smaller quantized model for tail.
Devin Khatri: Proposed config snippet for a route (draft):
```json
{
  "route": "/api/v1/generate",
  "max_tokens_cap": 2048,
  "tail_timeout_ms": 1200,
  "truncate_strategy": "smart_prefix_drop",
  "microbatch_cap": 4,
  "fallback_model": "redwood-small-quant"
}
```
Liam O'Connell: smart_prefix_drop explanation: when prefix length > X, drop least-recent conversational tokens (not system) until seq <= cap. Keeps system prompts intact. We can make it opt-in per tenant.
Akash Patel: For kernel stuff we can also add a short grace path: if kernel_init_time > threshold -> route to int8 kernel even if it's slightly slower throughput-wise, because it avoids init stalls that kill tail.
Maria Gomez: Can we make microbatch sizing dynamic by sequence length? Eg: microbatch_cap = max(1, min(8, floor(8192 / seq_len))). That reduces queues for long requests.
Devin Khatri: Nice. Draft formula: microbatch = clamp(1, 8, floor(8192 / max(1, seq_len))). Implemented as: `microbatch_cap = min(max_microbatch, floor(token_budget / seq_len))`. token_budget tuneable per hw class.
Ryan SRE: We need guardrails so this doesn't starve throughput. Proposal: apply dynamic microbatch only when route p99 > target AND average seq_len > threshold. Otherwise keep high batching.
BenchBot: experiment: dynamic-microbatch enabled on 10% traffic for long-seq routes -> p99 tail reduced 28% but overall throughput dropped 6%.
Liam O'Connell: Tradeoff expected. For hosted service we prefer lower p99 on tail workloads even at small throughput hit. For Dedicated customers maybe expose as toggle.
Akash Patel: Regarding KV cache: eviction churn seems high when many long seq requests force large KV allocations. Idea: soft-kv-eviction policy that prioritizes hot prefixes and allows ephemeral compression of KV for older contexts. Not trivial.
Maria Gomez: Short-term: let's implement route-level emergency caps: if predicted completion time > tail_timeout_ms -> return truncated response with metadata and a retry token. UX team ok with exposing truncated indicator.
Devin Khatri: Example response header: `X-Redwood-Truncated: true; truncation_reason=tail_protection; retry_token=...`
Ryan SRE: Also set client-visible rate-limiting headers so SDK can backoff.
Liam O'Connell: Action items:
- Akash: prototype soft-kv-eviction strategy (POC, perf tradeoffs) — due EOD+2.
- Devin: implement route config with `max_tokens_cap` + `tail_timeout_ms` and patch SDK to surface headers — due EOD+1.
- Maria: roll canary with dynamic microbatch on 5% for long-seq routes and collect p95/p99/tail metrics — start now.
- Ryan: add incident alert to pause canary if tail p99 increases > 100ms beyond baseline.
Akash Patel: Ack, starting POC.
Devin Khatri: Quick question on UX: do we prefer prefix or suffix drop? Our smart_prefix_drop keeps system + recent user turns; suffix drop would remove the most recent user tokens and is bad. So prefix seems better.
Maria Gomez: Agree. Also add telemetry to capture which tokens were dropped (hashed) so we can evaluate quality impact without storing PII.
BenchBot: perf-run (canary): dynamic-microbatch=on -> p95 -2ms, p99 -68ms, throughput -3.8% on long-seq. With `max_tokens_cap=2048` p99 -150ms but some user truncation rate = 4%.
Ryan SRE: Sounds reasonable. We should ship a conservative default: max_tokens_cap=4096 for general routes, 2048 for free-tier, and per-tenant opt-ins for >4096.
Liam O'Connell: Also add kernel-init telemetry: kernel_path, init_ms, used_batch_size. That will help route decisions.
Maria Gomez: Good call. Let's reconvene tomorrow after canary gathers 6h of data. If p99 stable, we'll roll to 25%.
Devin Khatri: I'll open a follow-up PR for the route schema and SDK headers.
Ryan SRE: Thanks all. If anyone sees a sudden spike before the canary finishes, ping #eng-oncall and tag me. :thumbsup:
Maria Gomez: SG, thanks.
Akash Patel: Leaving notes in the RFC doc: https://redwood.internal/rfc/tail-surge-protections (draft)
BenchBot: CI note: loadtest-2 failed 1/20 due to memory OOM on worker, investigating.
Liam O'Connell: OOM could be KV footprint, Akash pulled heap profiles.
Maria Gomez: Cool. End of thread for now — will post canary link soon.
